 Solo Leveling's New Cha Haein Confirms She 'Leveled Up' for the Netflix Series
 Han Sohee as Cha Haein in Netflix's Solo Leveling live-action K Drama series Brett Cardaro

 Brett Cardaro 
 Published Nov 17, 2026, 2:15 PM EST 
 Brett joined CBR's team in 2022 as a contributor before quickly moving into a staff writer and flex-editor role covering anime, video games and movies.

 Solo Leveling ’s Sung Jinwoo is gearing up for his most difficult challenge yet: the jump to live-action by way of Netflix’s new K Drama, which is currently in the middle of filming.

 Joining Sung Jinwoo actor Byeon Wooseok for the journey will be Han Sohee, who plays the female lead and powerful S-Rank South Korean Hunter Cha Haein. In anticipation of Haein’s live-action debut, Han Sohee did an interview with Elle in South Korea alongside a new photo shoot.
 If the images of Sohee rocking Haein’s signature short blonde hairstyle weren’t already convincing enough that she’s the ideal fit for the character, hearing how she talks about Haein with respect and appreciation should do the trick.
 Cha Haein Actress Han Sohee Reveals What She Learned From Stepping Into the Shoes of Solo Leveling's Female Lead
 Close Han Sohee in her shoot for Elle magazine in South Korea 
 Han Sohee in her shoot for Elle magazine in South Korea 
 Han Sohee in her shoot for Elle magazine in South Korea 
 “I’m in the middle of filming, so I don’t know Hae-in perfectly yet, but when I look into her heart, she is a more fragile person than anyone,” Sohee told Elle when asked about what she learned from diving deep into Cha Haein’s character . “She fights back to protect herself, but at the same time she strives to protect others and to live like a human being.”
 It’s true. While Haein is the second-strongest Hunter in South Korean (second only to Jinwoo himself), she is someone who is very firmly rooted in her humanity. She’s extremely down to earth, never seeing herself as a big star because of her powers. Haein solely uses her powers to help and protect others, which is more than can be said for many other awakened Hunters in her world.
 In the first episode of the Solo Leveling anime, for example, Haein’s introductory scene sees her helping return a woman’s purse after gracefully and effortlessly taking down some motorcycle bandits.
 “She’s a character who lives for the moment when everyone becomes happy. I don’t know if this is the right answer, but I always remind myself of that when I go to set.”
 Even despite having superhuman strength, Cha Haein deals with the same everyday struggles other people do. It seems that this more grounded aspect of Haein’s character is the one that Han Sohee embodies the most. Haein is very confident in her power as a Hunter , but she struggles with that same self-confidence when it comes to approaching matters of the heart. Stepping outside her comfort zone can be hard for Haein, because her power as a Hunter became a lonely road to walk at times.
 “In the past, I spent a lot of time alone,” Han Sohee laments, as though speaking from Haein’s own heart, “but I’ve come to realize that the most peaceful daily life is spending time with people who fill me up in colorful ways. Even when there’s nothing special, those times are precious. Even when the time gets boring, even when we end up telling the same stories again, time spent with the people I like and love is always enjoyable.”
 Han Sohee Is Taking Solo Leveling’s Strongest Female Hunter to Another Level
 Han Sohee as Cha Haein and Beyoen Wooseok as Sung Jinwoo in Netflix's Solo Leveling Image by Brett Cardaro 
 While Cha Haein is an extremely powerful Hunter, she can sometimes struggle with having the confidence to believe in herself. In those moments, it’s her fellow Hunters who inspire her, like when she promises to become stronger in order to catch up to Sung Jinwoo in the last episode of Solo Leveling Season 2 .
 “I want to catch up to him. I want to stand at his side. And to do that, I need to get stronger.”
 - Cha Haein
 Apparently, it’s the same for Sohee, who finds herself motivated by the admiration she has for her own peers: “Expressing acting and life earnestly and living them out is always my homework, and I worry a lot about how not to burn out. When I look around at those times, there are people living even more fiercely, and I think that’s how I was able to endure it together with them. Of course, today was no different.”
 Cha Haein may not be able to level up in the same way as Jinwoo , but she can still grow as a person and Hunter in her own way through hard work. To that end, she’s someone fans always see putting effort into improving throughout the webtoon, whether it’s by going on a daily run on a track, or taking sword training lessons from Song Chiyul.
 Cha Haein kills the Ant Queen in Solo Leveling Season 2 Episode 11 Image via A-1 Pictures 
 Han Sohee is also doing her best to ‘level up’ every day, just like Haein. “I think that with every project I’ve leveled up, slightly but little by little,” she tells Elle. “Living a character’s life is never easy, and even if it’s not 100%, I want to build it as far as my strength allows. In that process, sharing breath with senior actors and fellow actors puts me in a situation where I have no choice but to examine myself closely. Sometimes I even praise myself then.”
 It’s clear Han Sohee has taken on the role of Cha Haein with reverence for the character and the values she embodies: “So what improves over time, I suppose, is knowing exactly the weight I carry, accepting it humbly, and getting it done without complaint.”
 That sounds just like something Cha Haein would say.
 Netflix has yet to formally announce a release date for the live-action Solo Leveling series, but a recent report from Korean publication Naver suggests the show will come out some time in 2028.
